$comment: The anchored 0..4 rubric the metrics-report skill publishes for the host's annotation prompt (rubric-anchors.v1). scripts/lib/rubric.mjs enforces the scale and the dimension names; scripts/lib/registry.mjs holds the indicator categories. tests/rubric-anchors.test.mjs fails whenever this file and the code disagree. A quiet scene, a static character, a closed ending or a local cultural setting is never a defect by default: every rating is a claim about a passage in the selected text, not about the subject matter.

ratings.label: absent or broken
ratings.description: The requirement is not met: the reader cannot recover the relation or the feature at all, or the text works against it.

ratings.label: mostly failed
ratings.description: The requirement is met only intermittently; recovery is usually blocked, so the reader must supply what the text does not give.

ratings.label: partial
ratings.description: The requirement is met in places; recovery is possible but effortful, uneven or dependent on one fortunate cue.

ratings.label: reliable
ratings.description: The requirement is reliably met across the selection; the reader recovers the relation or the feature without strain, with at most minor gaps.

ratings.label: exact and economical
ratings.description: The requirement is met exactly and without waste; every needed relation or feature is recoverable and deliberate choices serve it rather than merely avoiding failure.

defaults.statement: A quiet scene, a static character, a closed ending or a local cultural setting is not a defect by default. Low tension is not low quality; a character who does not change can be the point of a scene; a deliberately closed ending can satisfy its promise; a local setting is a setting, not a demerit. Rate what the text does with its chosen material, and cite the passage that shows it.
defaults.justified_exception: A low rating on any dimension requires cited evidence that the chosen device fails its own purpose in the selected text, never the bare fact that the device was chosen.

referential_clarity.name: Referential clarity
referential_clarity.definition: Whether the reader can tell who and what each pronoun, name and definite description points at.
referential_clarity.evidence_question: Which referent or reference either resolves cleanly or stays ambiguous, and why? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: Referents are unrecoverable or shift without signal; the reader cannot tell who did what.
ratings.1: Most referents need guesswork; one or two pronouns never resolve.
ratings.2: Referents resolve unevenly; the reader must re-read to fix an antecedent.
ratings.3: Referents resolve reliably; at most a minor ambiguity remains deliberate.
ratings.4: Every referent resolves on first reading, and any ambiguity is visibly intended.

exceptions: A deliberately ambiguous referent is not a defect when the text signals the ambiguity and the ambiguity serves the scene.

discourse_connection.name: Discourse connection
discourse_connection.definition: Whether consecutive utterances and sentences are linked by recoverable relations rather than juxtaposed.
discourse_connection.evidence_question: Which connective relation (contrast, consequence, elaboration) links two adjacent passages, and where does a link break? Cite both.

ratings.0: Sentences follow one another with no recoverable relation; the paragraph reads as a list.
ratings.1: Links are mostly implicit and frequently unrecoverable.
ratings.2: Some links recover, others are jumps the reader must bridge alone.
ratings.3: Links recover reliably across the selection, with at most one abrupt join.
ratings.4: Every transition is motivated; juxtapositions that remain are intentional effects.

exceptions: Parataxis and montage can be deliberate; a rating of 4 does not require explicit connectives, only recoverable relations.

causal_support.name: Causal support
causal_support.definition: Whether events and choices are connected by recoverable causes and consequences.
causal_support.evidence_question: Which cause or consequence is visible in the text, and which asserted change lacks one? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: Events are asserted without causes; a change happens because the plot needs it.
ratings.1: Causes are named but not shown; motivation is a label.
ratings.2: Some events are motivated; one key change still rests on assertion.
ratings.3: Causes and consequences are recoverable; the text supplies what each turn needs.
ratings.4: Every consequential turn has a visible cause and cost, and nothing is over-explained.

exceptions: An unexplained event is not a defect when the narrator's or character's ignorance is the point and the text signals that the cause is withheld.

temporal_intelligibility.name: Temporal intelligibility
temporal_intelligibility.definition: Whether the reader can reconstruct the order and duration of events.
temporal_intelligibility.evidence_question: Which cue anchors the reader in time, and where does the order become unrecoverable? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: Order and duration are unrecoverable; events could have happened in any sequence.
ratings.1: Time is mostly unclear; the reader cannot place more than one event.
ratings.2: The order recovers with effort; one jump lacks an anchor.
ratings.3: The reader re-anchors reliably; a non-linear move is signalled and recoverable.
ratings.4: Order and duration are always recoverable, and non-linearity is a controlled effect.

exceptions: A deliberate time jump that keeps a recoverable anchor is high coherence, not a defect; a jump with no anchor is the failure.

perspective.name: Perspective
perspective.definition: Distinctiveness of the viewpoint or voice relative to the declared comparison scope.
perspective.evidence_question: What is distinctive about who is seeing or speaking, compared with the declared references? Cite the passage and name the comparison.

ratings.0: The viewpoint is interchangeable with any default narrator in the comparison scope.
ratings.1: The viewpoint is a familiar type with at most one distinguishing tic.
ratings.2: The viewpoint has a recognizable stance but leans on convention for most of its effect.
ratings.3: The viewpoint is distinctly held; its choices are its own and visible in the prose.
ratings.4: The viewpoint could not be swapped with a reference narrator without losing the scene.

exceptions: A familiar outsider viewpoint is not automatically low; distinctiveness is measured against the declared comparison scope, which must be named.

dramatic_development.name: Dramatic development
dramatic_development.definition: Distinctiveness of how the scene or turn unfolds, relative to the declared comparison scope.
dramatic_development.evidence_question: What is fresh about how the scene develops its pressure or turns, and what is borrowed? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: The development is the standard beat-for-beat shape of the genre, with nothing of its own.
ratings.1: One beat is rearranged; the rest follows the template.
ratings.2: The development has a recognizable twist but rests on familiar scaffolding.
ratings.3: The development is its own; the turn is earned by this scene's particulars.
ratings.4: The development could not be retold as a genre template without losing its point.

exceptions: A quiet scene whose pressure lives in small acts is a development, not a lack of development; do not reward added conflict by default.

expression.name: Expression
expression.definition: Distinctiveness of diction, syntax and imagery relative to the declared comparison scope.
expression.evidence_question: Which word, rhythm or image is this text's own, and which is borrowed? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: The expression is generic filler that could appear in any text of the comparison scope.
ratings.1: One image stands out; the rest is stock phrasing.
ratings.2: The expression is competent but familiar; freshness is occasional.
ratings.3: The expression is distinctly chosen; diction and rhythm serve this scene.
ratings.4: The expression is unmistakable; removing any image would change the text's effect.

exceptions: Plainness is not the same as cliché; precise plain prose and effective formal prose both rate on fit to the text, not on ornament.

novelty.name: Novelty of execution
novelty.definition: Freshness of execution relative to recent scene patterns and the declared comparison scope.
novelty.evidence_question: Which choice stages the material freshly, and where does it default to the expected? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: Every choice is the default for this kind of scene; nothing is freshly executed.
ratings.1: Freshness is isolated to a single detail; the rest is routine.
ratings.2: The scene has fresh staging in places but falls back on expectation elsewhere.
ratings.3: The execution is mostly fresh; familiar material is re-staged on purpose.
ratings.4: The execution is freshly staged throughout; the familiar is made to work, not to fill.

exceptions: A genre convention that works is useful, not a defect; novelty concerns execution, not whether the plot element is new.

cliche_reliance.name: Cliché reliance
cliche_reliance.definition: How much the effect depends on overused expression or machinery instead of earned, situated choices.
cliche_reliance.evidence_question: Which phrase or beat carries the effect by habit rather than by what the scene earns? Cite the passage.

ratings.0: Every effect rests on unearned reuse; the scene is made of ready-made parts.
ratings.1: The load-bearing beats are clichés; only the periphery is situated.
ratings.2: Cliché appears in places but is partly offset by situated choices.
ratings.3: Reuse is occasional and mostly earned by context; no load-bearing beat is a bare cliché.
ratings.4: No effect rests on unearned reuse; any recurring device gains meaning from context.

exceptions: A fixed phrase alone is a candidate for inspection, not proof of cliché; ritual repetition can gain meaning through context.

narrative_coherence.name: Narrative coherence
narrative_coherence.definition: Whether the reader can recover the causal, temporal and referential relations that make the account intelligible.
evidence_questions: Which relation works or fails, and how does the reader recover it? Cite the passage.
intended_effect_qualifications: Deliberate non-linearity is compatible with high coherence; an unreliable narrator is coherent when the contradiction is recoverable.

thematic_depth.name: Thematic depth
thematic_depth.definition: Whether choices and consequences support more than a repeated assertion about the theme.
evidence_questions: Which competing values or costs make a choice defensible in more than one way? Cite the choice and its cost.
intended_effect_qualifications: Abstract vocabulary and speeches about the theme do not establish depth; depth lives in the cost of a concrete choice.

character_complexity.name: Character complexity
character_complexity.definition: Whether wants, contradictions, defences and relationships are expressed through credible conduct.
evidence_questions: Which action reveals a want, a contradiction or a defence the surface would not predict? Cite the passage.
intended_effect_qualifications: A secondary character can be simple by design, and a static character can still reveal complexity as its scenes accumulate.

originality.name: Originality
originality.definition: What is distinctive about perspective, dramatic development or expression relative to the declared references.
evidence_questions: Which choice is this text's own, and against what declared reference? State the comparison limit.
intended_effect_qualifications: A familiar plot can be used freshly; distinctiveness is measured against the declared scope, not against all literature.

stylistic_quality.name: Stylistic quality
stylistic_quality.definition: Whether syntax, voice, attention and rhythm serve this particular text.
evidence_questions: Which exact passage shows the style working for the text, and where does it work against it? Cite it.
intended_effect_qualifications: Minimalism, formality and repetition need different contextual readings; a simpler register is not automatically weaker.

emotional_impact.name: Emotional impact
emotional_impact.definition: What specific action or detail supports investment or distance in the reader.
evidence_questions: Which situated action or detail invites the reader's investment or distance? Cite the passage.
intended_effect_qualifications: Constant distress is not strong impact; a predicted effect is not measured reader response, so keep the two apart.

interpretive_openness.name: Interpretive openness
interpretive_openness.definition: Which readings the text can support, and with what evidence.
evidence_questions: Which two or more readings does the text support, and on what evidence? Or which question does it deliberately close?
intended_effect_qualifications: Greater openness is not always better for the chosen book; a deliberately closed mystery that satisfies its promise is a success.

cultural_value.name: Cultural value
cultural_value.definition: Historical relevance and lasting influence, which a newly generated unpublished book cannot yet show.
evidence_questions: What reception or influence evidence exists? For a new book, state that it does not yet exist rather than predicting it.
intended_effect_qualifications: Return not_assessable for a new unpublished book; a local cultural setting is not inferior to a universal one.
